properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 8 at 7:22PM MDT until September 8 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
SVREPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northwestern Hidalgo County in southwestern New Mexico...

* Until 800 PM MDT.

* At 722 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 5 miles south of
Lordsburg, moving northwest at 15 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage
to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Lordsburg, Lordsburg Playa, Pyramid Mountains, and Shakespeare.

Blowing dust is likely to occur ahead of this storm.

This includes Interstate 10 in New Mexico between mile markers 9 and
30.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 8 at 11:01AM CDT until September 9 at 8:20PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Pine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake affecting Hardin and Jefferson
Counties.

...The Flood Warning is cancelled for the following rivers in
Texas...

Neches River at Neches River Saltwater Barrier affecting Hardin,
Jasper, Orange and Jefferson Counties.

For the Pine Island Bayou...including Sour Lake...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Pine Island Bayou near Sour Lake.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 25.0 feet, Water inundates roads in lowland areas near
the river. Low spots on Old Sour Lake Road are under water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:45 AM CDT Tuesday the stage was 26.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:45 AM CDT Tuesday was 27.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow morning and continue falling to 19.4 feet Sunday
morning.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 26.7
feet on 04/24/1977.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 1215 PM CDT.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 8 at 8:32PM CDT until September 8 at 9:15PM CDT by NWS Quad Cities IA IL
properties.description:
At 831 PM CDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from near Watkins to near Homestead to South English,
moving east at 45 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Cedar Rapids, Iowa City, Marengo, Marion, Coralville, North Liberty,
Mount Vernon, Williamsburg, Kalona, Lisbon, Fairfax, Solon, Tiffin,
Ely, Atkins, Walford, Wellman, University Heights, North English, and
Riverside.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 80 in Iowa between mile markers 211 and 251.
Interstate 380 between mile markers 1 and 23.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
sturdy building.

Continuous cloud to ground lightning is occurring with these storms.
Move indoors immediately. Lightning is one of nature's leading
killers. Remember, if you can hear thunder, you are close enough to
be struck by lightning.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with these storms, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 8 at 6:29PM CDT until September 9 at 12:30AM CDT by NWS Des Moines IA
properties.description:
FFWDMX

The National Weather Service in Des Moines has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Eastern Dallas County in central Iowa...
Polk County in central Iowa...

* Until 1230 AM CDT Wednesday.

* At 629 PM CDT, trained weather spotters reported thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches
of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is already
occurring.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Des Moines, West Des Moines, Ankeny, Urbandale, Johnston, Clive,
Altoona, Pleasant Hill, Grimes, Windsor Heights, Carlisle,
Bondurant, Polk City, Saylorville, Mitchellville, Adventureland
Amusement Park, Iowa State Fairgrounds and Prairie Meadows.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 80 between mile markers 121 and 149. Interstate 235 near
mile marker 1...and between mile markers 10 and 14...and between mile
markers 2 and 9. Interstate 35 between mile markers 100 and 102...and
between mile markers 68 and 99.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

For the latest stream observations and forecasts refer to
weather.gov/desmoines/water.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued September 8 at 9:26PM EDT until September 8 at 10:00PM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Bay and Gulf Side from Craig Key to Halfmoon Shoal out to 5
fathoms...
Gulf Waters from East Cape Sable to Chokoloskee 20 to 60 nm out and
beyond 5 fathoms...

* Until 1000 PM EDT.

* At 926 PM EDT, strong thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from near Gulfside 8 Reef to 8 nm north of Gulfside 9
Reef to 12 nm east of P Tower, moving southwest at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* Locations in the warning include...
P Tower, Gulfside 10 Reef, Gulfside 8 Reef, Gulfside 9 Reef,
Content Keys, and Gulfside 5 Reef.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, steep and fast-building
seas, frequent lightning, and blinding downpours. Stay low or go
below, and make sure all on board are wearing life jackets.
